_about: Known fixes at the game <-> system-library boundary, keyed by the imported NID. Per library function, never per game. Read by Ps5Backport.Core. Fields: kind (stub | swap | adapter | redirect | plt_stub = stub body in a cave and the PLT entry jumps to it, the GOT slot is left alone: forces a value even where the target firmware has the function | none = only in an option: removes the default fix for that NID), name, area, sources (keys of "sources" or free text), stub (a name in stubs.json, or "ret:<value>"), new_nid (swap/adapter target), new_library (optional target import library; reuse its existing library/module suffix), export_nid (redirect target, exported by the same module), insns (adapter code, one "hex  ; asm" per instruction, branch-free; "call_got" = call the real function through its GOT slot), when (missing = only when the import is missing on the target [default] | always = argument fixes), below (optional firmware: apply only when the target is lower, e.g. 5.00), post_call (adapter runs after the real function), proven (default true; false = derived, not console-tested), note, rationale. "options": opt-in groups (never applied by default; selected per backport). Each has name, description, warning, sources, group (where the app lists it; top-level "option_groups" orders the groups, unlisted groups follow) and its own fixes (a selected option's fixes replace the default fix for the same NID), optionally fakelib_variant (files in the fakelib set's <variant>/ subfolder replace the same-named fakelibs) and patterns (byte replacements: find/replace hex; in modules only 4-aligned hits inside non-executable segments, in the listed data files every hit). "patterns": byte replacements applied with the known fixes (name, area, sources, find/replace hex, code = search executable segments at any offset instead of 4-aligned data, note, rationale); the find bytes carry enough context to match one function only.

tU5e3f9gSiU.name: sceKernelIsTrinityMode
tU5e3f9gSiU.note: PS5 Pro query (libkernel from FW 7.00); 0 = not Pro

3WVD91e12ZQ.name: scePsmlMfsrInit
3WVD91e12ZQ.note: PSSR (MFSR) init skipped, reports 0x8a810012 (MFSR not supported), the native base-console answer
3WVD91e12ZQ.rationale: libScePsml first appears in FW 9.00. Most games call scePsmlMfsrInit only on a PS5 Pro (behind sceKernelIsTrinityMode or a Pro flag). Kingdom Come: Deliverance II calls sceSysmoduleLoadModule(0x137) and then scePsmlMfsrInit on every console, and its tester replaced the call with return 0. plt_stub because the Psml fakelib provides the function. The stub returns 0x8a810012 instead of 0: the native MfsrInit returns exactly that on a base console ('MFSR isn't supported in sceKernelIsTrinityMode() == 0', FW 12.70 libScePsml 0x2a85f), so every game shipped on base PS5s handles it, whereas success without initialisation makes every later Mfsr call return 0x8a810001 (not initialised). On a PS5 Pro (Trinity reported natively from FW 7.00) a sub-9.00 cook therefore skips PSSR cleanly (FINDINGS 6e). Lifted by the force_pro option (REFERENCE_OVERVIEW Part 28).

La9uyZv4Kvw.name: sceKernelGetAvailableCpumask
La9uyZv4Kvw.note: CPU affinity mask of the process (FW 12.40+): the firmware returns 0xff for a native title (0x1fff otherwise)
La9uyZv4Kvw.rationale: FW 12.70 libkernel computes the mask once from the app info: 0xff or 0x1fff, never 0 for a game. Callers pass it to thread-affinity calls; one game checks popcnt(mask) >= 5, so ret0 breaks it. A FW 4.03 backport (console-tested) returns 0xff; an earlier backport's ret0 only worked because its caller just forwards the value.

XgVs4jRehcY.name: sceKernelSyncOnAddressWait16
XgVs4jRehcY.rationale: Names from AnyPS5 (NIDs computed; not in aerolib). FreeBSD _umtx_op has no 8/16-bit compare, so Wait8/Wait16 stay return-0 stubs as in CONTROL (callers re-check and spin).

dFym5b41JLU.name: sceKernelSyncOnAddressWait8
dFym5b41JLU.rationale: Names from AnyPS5 (NIDs computed; not in aerolib). FreeBSD _umtx_op has no 8/16-bit compare, so Wait8/Wait16 stay return-0 stubs as in CONTROL (callers re-check and spin).

w7Ipp9Xl7hg.name: sceVideoOutAllowOutputResolutionWqhdDetection
w7Ipp9Xl7hg.note: no WQHD output detection: return 0 (FW 6.00 and later have it)

TViD1EZXkNI.name: sceAudioOut2Set3DLatency
TViD1EZXkNI.rationale: Absent before FW 6.00. FW 6.00-9.60 export it but accept latency 0-1 only (0x80268001 otherwise); latency 2 (user 0xff only) arrives in 10.01. Ghost of Yotei calls Set3DLatency(0xff, 2) during NCA setup: on FW 8.60 the refusal fails snd_SynthInit and the game crashes. A GOT stub is overwritten by the loader wherever the export exists, so the PLT entry is stubbed (FINDINGS 6b). Console-tested: Yotei FW 4.00 cook boots and plays on FW 8.60 (2026-10-13).

IXmfUaze9So.name: sceNpCommerceDialogOpen2
IXmfUaze9So.note: store dialog unavailable: returns an error (FW 7.00 and later have it)

fCWdlnmB1Ks.name: scePadIsRemoteController
fCWdlnmB1Ks.note: not a remote controller: *isRemote = 0, return 0 (FW 10.01 and later have it)
fCWdlnmB1Ks.rationale: BF6 4xx+ routes the PLT entry through a guard that calls the real function when its GOT slot is bound and otherwise does mov byte [rsi], 0; xor eax, eax; ret. The stub is that fallback.

D1IAo-CNswA.name: sceHttp2WebSocketSendDataMessage
D1IAo-CNswA.note: online disabled: returns an error (FW 5.02 and later have it)

jSHMX1oSE+E.name: sceHttp2WebSocketSendTextMessage
jSHMX1oSE+E.note: online disabled: returns an error (FW 5.02 and later have it)

v2hFBiyS13w.note: online disabled: returns an error (FW 5.02 and later have it)

bEegosRhgM0.name: sceHttp2SetRequestNoContentLength
bEegosRhgM0.note: FW 5.02 and later have it; marks an HTTP/2 request as having no Content-Length
bEegosRhgM0.rationale: A Unity PS5 player calls it once, only for a request without a known length (the other branch calls sceHttp2SetRequestContentLength), and ignores the result in both branches; that game's FW 4.xx backport left it unpatched (lazy binding: it fails only if called). Returning 0 skips the flag.

4h6F1LLbTiw.name: sceKernelMapNamedFlexibleMemoryInternal
4h6F1LLbTiw.note: -> sceKernelMapFlexibleMemory (name argument ignored), flags 0x8000 and 0x80000 cleared
4h6F1LLbTiw.rationale: libc's heap growth passes flags 0x8000, which only the internal entry accepts: the public sceKernelMapFlexibleMemory masks flags with 0xffbfff6f on FW 1.00-6.50 and rejects any bit of 0x88000 outright on FW 7.00-13.60 (test ecx, 0x88000), returning 0x80020016 (EINVAL), so a plain swap fails as soon as libc grows its heap ('Failed to create the heap', 0xa002000e). The swap is console-proven where that path was not taken; a FW 4.03 backport (console-tested) cleared the flag at both call sites, and so does this adapter. Every sample libc (SDK 9-13) passes exactly 0x8000; 0x80000 is cleared too so that a libc passing it cannot fail on 7.00+ (FINDINGS 6d).

B2n8aDorSH4.name: sceKernelSyncOnAddressWait32
insns: 4883ec10  ; sub rsp, 0x10   timespec on the stack; keeps rsp 16-aligned for the call
4989e0  ; mov r8, rsp   readable stand-in when there is no timeout
4885d2  ; test rdx, rdx   rdx = u32* timeout in microseconds, or NULL
410f95c2  ; setne r10b   r10 = 1 when a timeout was given
41f7f1  ; div r9d   eax = seconds, edx = remaining microseconds
4989e0  ; mov r8, rsp   uaddr2 = &timespec (relative timeout, uaddr = 0)
4d0f44c2  ; cmove r8, r10   no timeout -> uaddr2 = NULL
call_got  ; call _umtx_op through its GOT slot
B2n8aDorSH4.rationale: GT7's register transforms to _umtx_op op 11 (WAIT_UINT); CONTROL stubbed it to return 0. The timeout is a u32* in microseconds (Sony's own 12.70 implementation reads [rdx] and divides by 1000000; game libcs pass &u32 on their timed path, e.g. Yotei libc 0x1120b0). _umtx_op with uaddr = 0 reads uaddr2 as a struct timespec, so the adapter builds one on its stack (post-call, branch-free so it can be split across small caves) instead of passing the u32 pointer, which made timed waits read stack bytes as the timespec (FINDINGS 6d). The untimed path is the console-proven GT7 one; the timespec path is emulator-tested, not console-tested.

PZQhiiLXRFs.name: sceKernelSyncOnAddressWait64
insns: 4883ec10  ; sub rsp, 0x10   timespec on the stack; keeps rsp 16-aligned for the call
4989e0  ; mov r8, rsp   readable stand-in when there is no timeout
4885d2  ; test rdx, rdx   rdx = u32* timeout in microseconds, or NULL
410f95c2  ; setne r10b   r10 = 1 when a timeout was given
41f7f1  ; div r9d   eax = seconds, edx = remaining microseconds
4989e0  ; mov r8, rsp   uaddr2 = &timespec (relative timeout, uaddr = 0)
4d0f44c2  ; cmove r8, r10   no timeout -> uaddr2 = NULL
call_got  ; call _umtx_op through its GOT slot
PZQhiiLXRFs.rationale: GT7's register transforms to _umtx_op op 2 (WAIT); CONTROL stubbed it to return 0. The timeout is a u32* in microseconds (Sony's own 12.70 implementation reads [rdx] and divides by 1000000; game libcs pass &u32 on their timed path, e.g. Yotei libc 0x1120b0). _umtx_op with uaddr = 0 reads uaddr2 as a struct timespec, so the adapter builds one on its stack (post-call, branch-free so it can be split across small caves) instead of passing the u32 pointer, which made timed waits read stack bytes as the timespec (FINDINGS 6d). The untimed path is the console-proven GT7 one; the timespec path is emulator-tested, not console-tested.

q2y-wDIVWZA.name: sceKernelSyncOnAddressWake
q2y-wDIVWZA.rationale: GT7's exact register transforms to _umtx_op op 3 (WAKE); CONTROL stubbed it to return 0.

Hc4CaR6JBL0.name: sceKernelSyncOnAddressWait
insns: 4883ec10  ; sub rsp, 0x10   timespec on the stack; keeps rsp 16-aligned for the call
4989e0  ; mov r8, rsp   readable stand-in when there is no timeout
4885d2  ; test rdx, rdx   rdx = u32* timeout in microseconds, or NULL
410f95c2  ; setne r10b   r10 = 1 when a timeout was given
41f7f1  ; div r9d   eax = seconds, edx = remaining microseconds
4989e0  ; mov r8, rsp   uaddr2 = &timespec (relative timeout, uaddr = 0)
4d0f44c2  ; cmove r8, r10   no timeout -> uaddr2 = NULL
call_got  ; call _umtx_op through its GOT slot
Hc4CaR6JBL0.rationale: AnyPS5 shows the generic Wait has Wait32's signature (u32* addr, u32 expected, KernelUseconds* timeout, name), so it gets Wait32's translation (the console-proven Wait32 path, op 11 WAIT_UINT). GT7's own patch passed `expected` as the _umtx_op op code (spins instead of sleeping). The timeout is a u32* in microseconds (Sony's own 12.70 implementation reads [rdx] and divides by 1000000; game libcs pass &u32 on their timed path, e.g. Yotei libc 0x1120b0). _umtx_op with uaddr = 0 reads uaddr2 as a struct timespec, so the adapter builds one on its stack (post-call, branch-free so it can be split across small caves) instead of passing the u32 pointer, which made timed waits read stack bytes as the timespec (FINDINGS 6d). The 64-bit expected value and op question stays open (FINDINGS 1.6).

-sD02mFDBh4.name: sceUserServiceGetGamePresets
-sD02mFDBh4.rationale: Argument fix: newer SDKs pass a 0x30-byte struct (size field first); a FW 4.xx backport changed the game's size from 0x30 to 0x28 at its only call site. The size check is in the system service (the FW 4.03 library forwards the call over IPC), so the first firmware that accepts 0x30 is unknown; the original game runs on 11.xx, hence below 11.00. The game zeroes the struct first and reads back only the first 0x28 bytes. rax = [rsi]; if rax > 0x28: rax = 0x28; [rsi] = rax.

uv0Ae+jCeWY.name: sceHmd2ReprojectionSetAllowPositionalReprojection
uv0Ae+jCeWY.note: FW 6.50 and later have it; PSVR2 reprojection setting
uv0Ae+jCeWY.rationale: A PSVR2 game's FW 4.xx/5.xx backport wraps the import in a guard that returns 0 when the loader left it unresolved and calls the real function otherwise. A console-tested FW 4 backport of a game with an optional VR mode left it unpatched (never called without a headset); a VR-only game calls it, so returning 0 (success, setting ignored) is the fallback.

gWT7X8H0bYs.name: sceVideoOutGetOutputStatusWithVrr
gWT7X8H0bYs.note: VRR status getter (FW 10.01): zero the 0x50-byte status, i.e. VRR off
gWT7X8H0bYs.rationale: FW 10.01 libSceVideoOut: (handle, status*); the export returns an error without writing when VideoOut is not initialised or status is null, otherwise the implementation writes exactly 0x50 bytes (+0x00..+0x30 and a 32-byte block at +0x30). A game calling it ignores the return value and reads the struct (+0x04 == 2, bit 0x10 at +0x10, words at +0x30..+0x34), sometimes from uninitialised stack, so ret0 alone is not enough; an all-zero status takes the game's 'VRR off' path. Derived from the firmware code, not console-tested.

ubisoft_offline_popups.name: Ubisoft offline popups
ubisoft_offline_popups.description: Suppresses MUFFIN-4520 and MUFFIN-4521 using the existing silent-error callbacks in recognized Unity/Esut Ubisoft code. Detects linked code patterns without a game ID or fixed address.
ubisoft_offline_popups.warning: Opt-in. Requires Known fixes. Suppresses these two warnings only; online services remain unavailable when authentication fails. Tested on Rogue Prince of Persia; other matching games require console verification. Does not fix progress saving.
sources: Rogue Prince of Persia 01.006.000 PPSA28155: Ghidra analysis and console-confirmed popup suppression

unity_sku_offline.name: Unity unset-SKU offline fallback
unity_sku_offline.description: Allows recognized Unity/Esut authentication code to use its existing recoverable startup path when the platform reports an unset SKU. Detects linked code patterns rather than a game ID or fixed address; leaves trial and full-game results unchanged.
unity_sku_offline.warning: Opt-in. Console-tested on The Rogue Prince of Persia 01.006.000 (PPSA28155); other games require testing. Unrecognized or ambiguous code is left unchanged. Online-service warnings may still appear.
sources: The Rogue Prince of Persia 01.006.000 PPSA28155, user console-tested guarded NotSet fallback

boot_notice.name: Boot notification (Debug toast)
boot_notice.description: Redirects the eboot entry point into a cave that writes a user message to /dev/notification0 through the game's own imported libkernel functions (sceKernelOpen/sceKernelWrite/sceKernelClose, plus sceKernelUsleep for the delay), so the console renders it as a 'Debug:' toast after the configured delay, then jumps back to the real entry. The calls go through the game's PLT stubs, keeping the syscalls inside libkernel's text (a native_game process is killed for a direct syscall). The message text is baked into the eboot as immediate-encoded bytes (X-only text cannot hold string constants).
boot_notice.warning: Opt-in. Not console-tested: /dev/notification0 reachability from a game sandbox and toast rendering are unverified. Delays the whole eboot start by the delay (default 8 s); 0 disables the delay. Requires Known fixes.

save_mount_compat.name: Save mount compatibility
save_mount_compat.description: Changes sceSaveDataMount3 systemBlocks from -1 to 0 on target firmware below 5.00. Requires Known fixes enabled.
save_mount_compat.warning: Disabled by default. Derived adapter, not console-tested. Without it, old firmware may reject a save-mount request using -1. Disabling does not undo patches already present in the input.
sources: Existing save-data argument adapter; console testing pending

ZP4e7rlzOUk.name: sceSaveDataMount3
ZP4e7rlzOUk.rationale: Argument fix: the function exists on old firmware but rejects values newer SDKs pass (AC README: ShellCore rejects -1 when the game SDK is below 5.00, hence below 5.00). All three games patched this at the call site in their own code; doing it at the import boundary covers every game. rax = [rdi+0x18]; r11 = rax+1; if r11 == 0 (value was -1): rax = 0; [rdi+0x18] = rax.

save_prepare_compat.name: Save preparation compatibility
save_prepare_compat.description: Changes sceSaveDataPrepare preparation mode 2 to 1 before the native call. Requires Known fixes enabled.
save_prepare_compat.warning: Disabled by default. Derived adapter, not console-tested. Without it, the native save-preparation call may reject mode 2. Disabling does not undo patches already present in the input.
sources: Existing save-data argument adapter; console testing pending

sDCBrmc61XU.name: sceSaveDataPrepare
sDCBrmc61XU.rationale: Argument fix (CONTROL patched the call site). eax = [rsi+4]; if eax == 2: eax = 1; [rsi+4] = eax (r11 scratch).

audio_speaker_compat.name: Audio speaker compatibility
audio_speaker_compat.description: Limits the reported speaker configuration to eight speakers and clears the 3D-audio flag after sceAudioOut2GetSpeakerInfo. Optional so dialogue issues can be compared with this adapter enabled or disabled. Requires Known fixes enabled.
audio_speaker_compat.warning: Experimental; this adapter is derived and not console-tested. Disabled by default. Without it, some old-SDK games may select an unsupported audio layout and lose sound. Required missing audio API stubs and other existing audio fixes remain active. Re-cook from the same source for each test; disabling does not undo patches already present in the input.

DImz2Ft9E2g.name: sceAudioOut2GetSpeakerInfo
insns: 57  ; push rdi (SpeakerInfo*; also aligns the stack)
call_got  ; call the real function through its GOT slot
DImz2Ft9E2g.rationale: On newer firmware the OS reports 3D audio / 7.1.4 speakers, the game then opens a 12-channel AudioOut2 port, and an old-SDK binary is refused: no sound (CONTROL README; CONTROL fixed it inside Wwise). The game decides from GetSpeakerInfo (CONTROL eboot 0x3ca27f1: flags & 1 = 3D audio, popcnt(available_bits) > 8 = height speakers; struct layout from AnyPS5). Post-call fix: run the real function, then clear the 3D flag and cap the report at 8 speakers. Derived from references, not console-tested.

audio_port_compat.name: Audio port compatibility
audio_port_compat.description: Turns a 12-channel (7.1.4) main sceAudioOut2 port into an 8-channel (7.1) one and folds the game's 12-channel audio into it every grain (height channels mixed into the front and back pairs), so old-SDK cooks of games with 7.1.4 output start and sound right. Applies to targets below 11.00. Requires Known fixes enabled.
audio_port_compat.warning: Experimental, not console-tested yet. Ghost of Yotei (SDK 4.00 cook) needs it to start on FW 13.60; the earlier rewrite-only version crackled, this version adds the downmix. Code is placed in the code-space extension and keeps 0x48 bytes of state in the last data page. Disabled by default. Re-cook from the same source for each test; disabling does not undo patches already present in the input.

0x6o1VVAYSY.name: sceAudioOut2ContextCreate
0x6o1VVAYSY.note: AudioOut2ContextParam.num_grains (+0x10) saved as the grain length of the 12->8 downmix
0x6o1VVAYSY.rationale: Part of the 12->8 channel downmix (with sceAudioOut2PortCreate, PortSetAttributes, ContextAdvance and PortDestroy). A port's PCM buffer holds one grain of frames; the grain is the context's num_grains (AnyPS5 AudioOut2ContextParam: max_ports, max_object_ports, guarantee_object_ports, queue_depth, num_grains, flags; 0 means 256). State 'audio_out2_downmix' (0x48 bytes, zero at load, shared by the five rules): +0 u32 grain (frames, from the last sceAudioOut2ContextCreate num_grains, 256 for 0); +4 u32 bitmask of slots folded in the current grain; +8 8 x u64 handles of ports rewritten from 12 to 8 channels (0 = free; 8 slots: Ghost of Yotei keeps at most 3 bed ports plus the probe port open, and the 0x48 bytes fit the 0x58-byte page tail of EA eboots such as Battlefield 6).

JK2wamZPzwM.name: sceAudioOut2PortCreate
JK2wamZPzwM.note: AudioOut2PortParam.data_format (+4): 12-channel float main port (0xC00) -> 8 channels (0x800); the new port is remembered for the downmix
JK2wamZPzwM.rationale: An old-SDK binary is refused a 12-channel (7.1.4) main port with 0x8026800E (unsupported format) on FW 13.60, and FW 4.00's libSceAudioOut accepts only 2, 8 or 10 channels for main ports (channel mask 0x504 in sceAudioOut2LoPortCreate), while 8 channels are accepted everywhere. Ghost of Yotei's Scream/NCA always builds 7.1.4 bed ports (snd_SynthInit sets NCA parameter 1 = 0x3fff; FINDINGS Part 1 section 6a); refused, snd_SynthInit failed and the game crashed. The rewrite alone made 8-channel ports carry 12-channel frames (crackle); the companion rules fold the data. Post-call: only for port_type 0 and data_format & 0xfff == 0xC00 (float), the field is rewritten in place (the caller's descriptor then says 8 channels, so its gain attribute has 8 entries) and, when the call succeeds, the returned handle goes into a free slot (8 slots; more ports stay unfolded). State 'audio_out2_downmix' (0x48 bytes, zero at load, shared by the five rules): +0 u32 grain (frames, from the last sceAudioOut2ContextCreate num_grains, 256 for 0); +4 u32 bitmask of slots folded in the current grain; +8 8 x u64 handles of ports rewritten from 12 to 8 channels (0 = free; 8 slots: Ghost of Yotei keeps at most 3 bed ports plus the probe port open, and the 0x48 bytes fit the 0x58-byte page tail of EA eboots such as Battlefield 6).

8XTArSPyWHk.name: sceAudioOut2PortSetAttributes
8XTArSPyWHk.note: PCM of a rewritten port folded in place from 7.1.4 to 7.1 (once per grain); a 12-entry gain attribute trimmed to 8
8XTArSPyWHk.rationale: For a port whose handle the sceAudioOut2PortCreate rule remembered: attribute 0 (value = 8 bytes holding the PCM buffer pointer, AnyPS5) -> the buffer's grain x 12 float frames are folded in place to grain x 8: channels 0-7 kept, heights 8/9 (top front L/R) added to 0/1 and 10/11 (top rear L/R) to 6/7 at 0.7071 (AnyPS5's 12-channel order: L R C LFE Ls Rs Lb Rb TFL TFR TRL TRR). Once per port and grain (bitmask cleared by the sceAudioOut2ContextAdvance rule), so a second PCM set in the same grain does not fold twice. Attribute 1 (gains) of size 48 becomes 32. Data is final at this call: the library reads the buffer at this call or later, and NCA renders before it submits attributes (vtable +0x48 0x74e6b0 sets attributes, then advances). In place is safe: frame f is read whole before its 8 floats are written at 32*f <= 48*f. Other ports and attributes are untouched. State 'audio_out2_downmix' (0x48 bytes, zero at load, shared by the five rules): +0 u32 grain (frames, from the last sceAudioOut2ContextCreate num_grains, 256 for 0); +4 u32 bitmask of slots folded in the current grain; +8 8 x u64 handles of ports rewritten from 12 to 8 channels (0 = free; 8 slots: Ghost of Yotei keeps at most 3 bed ports plus the probe port open, and the 0x48 bytes fit the 0x58-byte page tail of EA eboots such as Battlefield 6).

PE2zHMqLSHs.name: sceAudioOut2ContextAdvance
PE2zHMqLSHs.note: a new grain starts: the downmix's per-grain fold marks are cleared
PE2zHMqLSHs.rationale: Part of the 12->8 channel downmix: clears the bitmask that keeps the sceAudioOut2PortSetAttributes rule to one fold per port and grain. State 'audio_out2_downmix' (0x48 bytes, zero at load, shared by the five rules): +0 u32 grain (frames, from the last sceAudioOut2ContextCreate num_grains, 256 for 0); +4 u32 bitmask of slots folded in the current grain; +8 8 x u64 handles of ports rewritten from 12 to 8 channels (0 = free; 8 slots: Ghost of Yotei keeps at most 3 bed ports plus the probe port open, and the 0x48 bytes fit the 0x58-byte page tail of EA eboots such as Battlefield 6).

cd+Rtw+D1x8.name: sceAudioOut2PortDestroy
cd+Rtw+D1x8.note: a destroyed port is removed from the downmix's port list
cd+Rtw+D1x8.rationale: Part of the 12->8 channel downmix: frees the handle's slot, so a later port that reuses the handle value or the buffer is not folded by mistake. State 'audio_out2_downmix' (0x48 bytes, zero at load, shared by the five rules): +0 u32 grain (frames, from the last sceAudioOut2ContextCreate num_grains, 256 for 0); +4 u32 bitmask of slots folded in the current grain; +8 8 x u64 handles of ports rewritten from 12 to 8 channels (0 = free; 8 slots: Ghost of Yotei keeps at most 3 bed ports plus the probe port open, and the 0x48 bytes fit the 0x58-byte page tail of EA eboots such as Battlefield 6).

audio_bed_71.name: Audio 7.1 bed (engine)
audio_bed_71.description: Makes the Scream/NCA audio engine render its main output as 7.1 instead of 7.1.4: the engine's permitted output modes lose the 7.1.4 bit, the start-up probe asks for an 8-channel port, and the reported output channel count is capped at 8. The engine then builds 8-channel beds itself (the path its music outputs already use), so no per-grain conversion runs. Alternative to Audio port compatibility (the 12->8 downmix); select one. Applies to targets below 11.00. Requires Known fixes enabled.
audio_bed_71.warning: Experimental, not console-tested. Height channels are dropped rather than mixed into the bed. Only games whose engine matches the byte patterns (Ghost of Yotei's Scream build) are changed; the channel cap alone is harmless elsewhere. Cannot be combined with Audio port compatibility. Re-cook from the same source for each test; disabling does not undo patches already present in the input.

patterns.name: Scream permitted output modes 7.1.4 -> 7.1
patterns.note: snd_SynthInit SetParam(kProperty_OutputModesPermitted, 0x3fff) -> 0x3fef: bit 0x10 (7.1.4) is read only by NCA's bed-channel selection, so the main beds become 8-channel (format 0x880, the BGM ports' format)

patterns.name: NCA probe port 12 -> 8 channels
patterns.note: the start-up speaker probe's AudioOut2PortParam constant (48000 Hz, data_format 0xC00) -> 0x800; a 12-channel main port is refused for an old-SDK caller on FW 13.60 and for everyone below 11

gatEUKG+Ea4.name: sceAudioOut2PortGetState
gatEUKG+Ea4.note: AudioOut2PortState.num_channels (+2) capped at 8 after a successful call, so the engine never selects 7.1.4 for an 8-channel bed
gatEUKG+Ea4.rationale: Part of the 7.1 bed option: with the beds built as 8 channels, a console that reports a 12-channel output (FW 13.60 with a 7.1.4 layout) would still make Scream pick the 7.1.4 playback mode, and NCA writes a 7.1.4 mix into an 8-channel bed through its generic fallback. Capping the reported count keeps the mode at 7.1, which the 8-channel bed path renders directly. The adapter forwards the call unchanged and edits the result only when the call succeeded and a state pointer was given. The one-adapter console test on FW 13.60 (T4, FINDINGS Part 1 section 6a) found this cap harmless on its own.

auto_pro.name: Automatic Pro mode
auto_pro.description: Keeps native console-mode queries when available, so the game can choose its base PS5 or PS5 Pro path at runtime. Missing queries fall back to base-console values. Keeps the default Psml initialization guard below firmware 9.00. Requires Known fixes enabled.
auto_pro.warning: Experimental; test on both console types. Queries missing from the selected target fall back to fixed base-console answers, even if this cook later runs on a Pro with newer firmware. Preserves automatic selection only for queries the target supports. Replacement libraries must report the actual console correctly. Cannot be combined with Force PS5 Pro mode.
sources: Native hardware queries with base-console fallback; console testing pending

NH6xARDOVv8.name: sceKernelGetOperationMode
NH6xARDOVv8.note: Only missing queries return normal mode; native queries are unchanged.

tU5e3f9gSiU.name: sceKernelIsTrinityMode
tU5e3f9gSiU.note: Only missing queries return not Pro; native queries are unchanged.

yu17wG8L5FI.name: sceKernelHasTrinityMode
yu17wG8L5FI.note: Only missing queries return not Pro; native queries are unchanged.

BfBDZGbti7A.name: sceAgcGetIsTrinityMode
BfBDZGbti7A.note: Only missing queries write a one-byte false flag; native queries are unchanged.

force_pro.name: Force PS5 Pro mode
force_pro.description: Makes the game treat the console as a PS5 Pro (Pro graphics mode, PSSR when the game supports it): sceKernelGetOperationMode reports mode 3, sceKernelIsTrinityMode and sceAgcGetIsTrinityMode report true, and scePsmlMfsrInit is called again (the default skips it below FW 9.00).
force_pro.warning: PS5 Pro only. On a base PS5 or Slim, or on a Pro firmware where the game's PSSR path fails, the game shows a black screen. PSSR may also need a newer libScePsml fakelib and the PSSR model file.

BfBDZGbti7A.name: sceAgcGetIsTrinityMode
BfBDZGbti7A.note: *(bool*)out = 1, return 1 (as sceAgcGetIsTrinityMode on a real PS5 Pro)

3WVD91e12ZQ.name: scePsmlMfsrInit
3WVD91e12ZQ.note: keeps the real init (PSSR needs it)

gpu_scratch.name: GPU compute scratch fix (firmware below 12)
gpu_scratch.description: Uses the fakelib set's libSceAgcDriver variant that hooks command-buffer submission and gives compute shaders a 24 MB scratch area (older firmware sets none up), and turns every s_trap 1 (asserts in the SDK's ray-tracing BVH shaders) into s_nop in the game's modules and ShaderData.bin.
gpu_scratch.warning: Not needed by most games. Use it when a game hangs or shows a black screen during GPU work on firmware below 12. Needs a fakelib set with a gpu_scratch variant (fakelibs/4, fakelibs/4.03).

playgo_0_6.name: PlayGo 0.6 (experimental)
playgo_0_6.description: Replaces libScePlayGo.sprx with the official 0.6 build, adding synchronized lifecycle handling and empty-list compatibility. Keeps the current library unless selected.
playgo_0_6.warning: Console compatibility is unverified. Available in the 4, 4.03, 7, 9.60, 10 and 11 store sets. Select either this option or PlayGo 0.6 logging. Uses an existing /app0/playgo_stub.dat when present; no config is generated.

playgo_0_6_log.name: PlayGo 0.6 logging (experimental)
playgo_0_6_log.description: Uses the official 0.6 logging build under the runtime name libScePlayGo.sprx. Writes /app0/playlgo.log (upstream spelling) for one diagnostic run.
playgo_0_6_log.warning: Console compatibility is unverified. Logging changes timing and writes /app0/playlgo.log (upstream spelling). Available in the 4, 4.03, 7, 9.60, 10 and 11 store sets. Select either this option or normal PlayGo 0.6; collect the log and disable this option after testing. No config is generated.

psml_kpn9.name: PSSR model as KPN9_v070.psp (experimental)
psml_kpn9.description: Uses the fakelib set's libScePsml variant that loads the PS5 Pro PSSR model from /app0/KPN9_v070.psp (its FW 13.60 system name) instead of /app0/k9.psp. The same FW 13.60 model file is added under that name.
psml_kpn9.warning: Not console-tested. Only matters on a PS5 Pro for a game that uses PSSR. Available in the 4 and 9.60 store sets.

np_error_dialogs.name: Hide PSN error dialogs
np_error_dialogs.description: Keeps the system 'Something went wrong' box for PlayStation Network and network errors off the screen: sceErrorDialogOpen returns success without opening the dialog when the error code's facility is NP (0x8055xxxx) or libSceNet (0x8041xxxx), and the next sceErrorDialogUpdateStatus / sceErrorDialogGetStatus reports the dialog as finished, so the game continues as if the user had dismissed it. Other error codes open the real dialog. Applies to every target firmware. Requires Known fixes enabled.
np_error_dialogs.warning: Opt-in. Not console-tested. Hides genuine PSN and network errors too; only for consoles that cannot reach PSN. Covers games that report online errors through the system error dialog (libSceErrorDialog); a game's own message box is unchanged, and a game that waits for PSN before continuing still waits. Keeps one byte of state in the last data page.

M2ZF-ClLhgY.name: sceErrorDialogOpen
insns: c605{state+0x0}01  ; mov byte ptr [rip + state+0x0], 1 (dialog suppressed)
c605{state+0x0}00  ; mov byte ptr [rip + state+0x0], 0 (real dialog: clear)
M2ZF-ClLhgY.note: NP (0x8055xxxx) and net (0x8041xxxx) error codes are not shown: returns 0 and marks the dialog as suppressed; other codes clear the mark and open the real dialog
M2ZF-ClLhgY.rationale: Ghost of Yotei's NP sign-in code queues every failed NpManager/NpAuth result for sceErrorDialogOpen (FINDINGS 6a: NP-104602-3 = 0x8055A011, the code ShellCore gives pending NP requests when a sign-in fails, which a console that cannot reach PSN produces at every boot). The game only expects the dialog to finish, so answering at the import boundary leaves its logic unchanged and works for any game that uses the system error dialog. Facility, not code: ShellCore's display-code table maps the whole 0x8055A0xx server-request range to NP-1045xx..1046xx.

WWiGuh9XfgQ.name: sceErrorDialogUpdateStatus
WWiGuh9XfgQ.note: after a suppressed sceErrorDialogOpen the first status poll reports FINISHED and clears the mark; otherwise the real function
WWiGuh9XfgQ.rationale: Games poll the status until the dialog finishes (Ghost of Yotei accepts only RUNNING = keep waiting, FINISHED = done); with no real dialog open the system would report NONE or INITIALIZED, on which some games spin. Reporting FINISHED once completes the game's dialog state machine the way a user dismissal does.

t2FvHRXzgqk.name: sceErrorDialogGetStatus
t2FvHRXzgqk.note: same as sceErrorDialogUpdateStatus for games that poll the non-updating status query
t2FvHRXzgqk.rationale: Part of the Hide PSN error dialogs option; either status call may be the one a game polls after sceErrorDialogOpen.

ekXHb1kDBl0.name: sceErrorDialogClose
ekXHb1kDBl0.note: closing a dialog clears the suppressed mark, then the real function runs
ekXHb1kDBl0.rationale: Part of the Hide PSN error dialogs option: a game that closes a suppressed dialog without polling its status must not see the next real dialog reported as finished at once.

patterns.name: Wwise 7.1.4 -> 7.1 (speaker setup)
patterns.note: Wwise speaker setup: 7.1.4 (12 channels) -> 7.1, which an SDK-4 binary can open
patterns.rationale: A newer OS reports 3D audio, so Wwise picks 7.1.4 (channel mask 0x2d63f10c); a port opened by a low-SDK binary is refused at 12 channels and there is no sound. The mask becomes 7.1 (0x63f108). Same Wwise build in CONTROL (patched the speaker-setup site), Beast of Reincarnation and Borderlands 4 (both sites; BL4 also the packed default below).

patterns.name: Wwise 7.1.4 -> 7.1 (channel switch)
patterns.note: Wwise speaker setup: 7.1.4 (12 channels) -> 7.1, which an SDK-4 binary can open
patterns.rationale: A newer OS reports 3D audio, so Wwise picks 7.1.4 (channel mask 0x2d63f10c); a port opened by a low-SDK binary is refused at 12 channels and there is no sound. The mask becomes 7.1 (0x63f108). Same Wwise build in CONTROL (patched the speaker-setup site), Beast of Reincarnation and Borderlands 4 (both sites; BL4 also the packed default below).

patterns.name: Wwise 7.1.4 -> 7.1 (packed default)
patterns.note: Wwise speaker setup: 7.1.4 (12 channels) -> 7.1, which an SDK-4 binary can open
patterns.rationale: movabs rdx, 0x2d63f10c2d63f10c (two 7.1.4 masks) stored as a default; Borderlands 4 changes the low one to 7.1 (0x63f108). CONTROL and Beast left it, so it is the least proven of the three Wwise sites.

patterns.name: EA Sports Frostbite: 0x30c output buffer 0xc00 -> 0x800
patterns.note: probably 12 -> 8 audio channels (format 0x30c), the Frostbite counterpart of the Wwise 7.1.4 -> 7.1 fix
patterns.rationale: In the branch taken when a global format equals 0x30c (read as type 3, 12 channels; 0x201 nearby), a size field [rbp-0xf0] is set to 0xc00 (12 x 0x100); both EA Sports backports set 0x800 (8 x 0x100). The meaning is inferred from the values, not traced. UFC 6 tested on a PS5 Pro at FW 9.60; FC 27 ships it in both its backports. Not in Battlefield 6 (different code).
